events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $7.11 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The dispute is a route deviation on a RydeTAXI trip. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists [F3] and that no traffic incident excuses it: the only traffic records are speed bands, and RD-4(b) speed bands do not exempt on their own, with the incident screen failing [F12][F15][RD-4]. The complaint and the driver's own post-trip statement both confirm the driving was off the agreed road [F11], so the only live question is RD-5 consent scope for the segment [F3].

On RD-5, the rider's message is a specific-route grant, not a general one: the driver asked "can I go round via Upper Paya Lebar Road?" and the rider answered "Sure, no problem." [F8][F9]. That covers driving on Upper Paya Lebar Road only. The driver's statement says "In the end I went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead … same direction" [F11] — the record thus places the driven segment on a different road from the one consented to, so the agreement does not cover this segment; it counts under RD-5 [F8][F9][F11][RD-5]. RD-3 does not help either: no rider-named stop was requested or driven, so RD-3(a) has no application and the segment-specific extra km is not excused [F3][RD-3]. The RD-4(b) band 2 reading on KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY [F12] is at most supporting colour for the driver's claimed jam and does not exempt.

Amount under RD-2 for a RydeTAXI trip: the rate is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km, $26.30 ÷ 18.65 km = $1.4102/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The excess-distance fact already states the segment's extra km — $7.50 ÷ $1.4102/km = 5.3189 km, i.e. the 5.04 km segment plus corridor/matching difference [F3][F4]. Only the non-exempt segment's extra km is refundable: 5.04 km × $1.4102/km = $7.1074 → $7.11 [F3][F4][RD-2]. Waiting billed on this metered taxi trip ($0.11, 0.4 min) stands under RD-3(c) [F5][RD-3]. No surge applied [F6]. The fraction of extra km not attributable to the segment (the ~0.28 km between $7.50 and the segment) is not refunded per RD-2 [F3][F4][RD-2]. No flag_account: the prior-upheld route-dispute screen fails (route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0), so RD-6's repeated-breach condition is not met [F18][RD-6]. Safety screen: the chat, the driver statement and the complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation — nothing arises [F8][F9][F11][F13][SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $7.11 to the rider (metered-distance overcharge for the non-exempt off-route segment, per NS-7); no account flag — driver has no prior upheld route dispute.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Your dispute is resolved: you get a $7.11 Ryde voucher.

What decided it: your trip went off the road you'd agreed to. You OK'd driving via Upper Paya Lebar Road, but the driver's own account says the car went by Hougang Avenue 3 instead, so that stretch wasn't covered by your agreement and you were charged for the extra distance. Traffic alone doesn't excuse it.

The voucher covers the distance you were overcharged on that stretch; the small remainder of the extra distance isn't refunded, and the waiting charge stands.

Nothing changes on your account. The voucher is applied as Ryde credit.

DRIVER: Outcome: a $7.11 Ryde voucher goes to the rider.

Why: the trip included an off-route stretch. The rider agreed to Upper Paya Lebar Road, but your statement says you drove via Hougang Avenue 3 instead, so the consent didn't cover that stretch and the metered distance for it is refunded. Traffic conditions don't exempt an off-route stretch on their own.

The waiting amount and the rest of the extra distance stay as billed.

No account flag is applied, and no mark goes on your record — you have no prior upheld route disputes.
